### executor/implement-spec (v6ba2f814dd6f)
## Trigger
Any execute task from the orchestrator.

## Objective
Implement one atomic task within its Scope and leave tests green.

## Procedure
Read Spec, Acceptance, Scope. Run `scripts/tests_green.sh` first. Make the smallest accepted change. Run it again; iterate on failure. Commit on the task branch.

## Tools
Read, Edit, Bash; `scripts/failures_only.sh`.

## Evidence requirements
Acceptance checks and tests-green result.

## Output contract
Finish with: 3-line summary, `git diff --stat`, failures-only output (empty when green).

## Stop conditions
Stop when Acceptance passes or budget ends.

## Failure/recovery
Report only `scripts/failures_only.sh` output. Edit only paths in Scope. No new dependencies unless the spec names them.
## objective
TestFlight prep: production API base for native builds, Info.plist encryption flag, build number 2, icon alpha check, cap sync
- discovery: Prepare the Capacitor iOS app (ios/App, bundle id ch.alltag.app) for a TestFlight upload. No signing, no archive, no upload, no Apple account access, no keychain access: the human does those in Xcode.
1. Production API base: the native app is served from https://localhost, so relative /api calls fail. Add `.env.production` with `VITE_API_BASE=https://alltag-xi.vercel.app` (a public URL, not a secret) unless the app already resolves the API base another way for native builds; check src for how VITE_API_BASE is read and make sure Capacitor builds use it. Keep docs/readme.test.ts green (every .env.example var appears in README).
2. Info.plist (ios/App/App/Info.plist): add `ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption` = false (only standard HTTPS); keep NSCameraUsageDescription and NSMicrophoneUsageDescription; if the app uses speech recognition (grep for SpeechRecognition / webkitSpeechRecognition), add NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription "alltag checks what you say in review".
3. project.pbxproj: CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION 1 -> 2 for both configurations; MARKETING_VERSION stays 1.0. Do NOT set DEVELOPMENT_TEAM.
4. App icon: confirm ios/App/App/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset has a 1024x1024 PNG without alpha (App Store rejects alpha). If it has alpha, flatten it onto the linen #F4F2EE background with macOS `sips` and replace it.
5. Run `pnpm install`, `pnpm build`, `npx cap sync ios`. Commit the resulting changes to ios/ that cap sync produces (public assets are usually gitignored; follow the repo's .gitignore).
6. Gate: `npm test -- --watch=false`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint` green.
7. Result: list what changed, and confirm `xcodebuild -project ios/App/App.xcodeproj -scheme App -configuration Release -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build` succeeds (simulator build, no signing) so the human's Archive will compile.
Rollback: git revert the commit.

- Native build calls https://alltag-xi.vercel.app/api (VITE_API_BASE set for production builds)
- Info.plist has ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption false and all needed usage descriptions; CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION 2; no DEVELOPMENT_TEAM set
- AppIcon 1024 has no alpha; cap sync ios done; unsigned Release simulator xcodebuild succeeds
- Gate green: npm test -- --watch=false, npx tsc --noEmit, npm run lint

The same web build runs as a native iOS app (`ios/`, Swift Package Manager, no CocoaPods). The web app on Vercel stays the main deliverable.

Prerequisites: a Mac with Xcode 26 and an Apple ID. A free personal team is enough to run on your own iPhone; the build then expires after 7 days and needs a fresh Run.

```sh
pnpm i
VITE_API_BASE=https://<your-vercel-host> pnpm ios:build   # vite build && cap sync ios
pnpm ios:open                                              # opens ios/App in Xcode
```

In Xcode pick your team under Signing & Capabilities, select your iPhone, press Run.

- `VITE_API_BASE` must be set (in `.env` or inline as above) before `ios:build`. Without it the native app calls its own origin (`https://localhost/api/...`) and every request fails.
- On that Vercel deployment set `ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://localhost`, otherwise CORS blocks the app and the token routes answer 403.
- Camera and microphone prompts appear on first use.
- Limits: WebGPU inside WKWebView on iOS 26 is untested, so the on-device Gemma fallback may not work in the native shell. The PWA on Android Chrome is the tested offline path.

E
